en: Mayon Volcano has a perfectly symmetrical cone shape that you can easily see from Legazpi City.
Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features observable limestone stalactites and stalagmites inside its massive cave.
The vast mudflats of Manila Bay become completely exposed and walkable during low tide.
The Rafflesia schadenbergiana, found in Mount Kitanglad, produces massive, foul-smelling red flowers observable in the mossy forest.
The southwest monsoon, locally called Habagat, brings heavy, observable rainfall and dark clouds to the western Philippines.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park contains visible, colorful coral reefs teeming with marine life in the Sulu Sea.
Mount Pulag's summit is frequently covered by a thick, observable sea of clouds above the tree line.
Maria Cristina Falls in Iligan City displays a massive, observable double-drop waterfall powered by the Agus River.
The white sand of Boracay's White Beach is composed of finely crushed coral and marine organisms.
The Cagayan River forms a massive, observable river delta where it empties into the Babuyan Channel.
Tiwi in Albay features observable natural hot springs heated by the underground magma of Mount Malinao.
You can observe the unique chocolate-colored hills of Bohol turning brown during the dry season.
